findings.note: The Codex judge arm has neither a per-call timeout nor the retry ladder the HTTP arm uses. internal/fsm/judge/codex.go:64 calls j.exec with the caller's ctx and sets v.Attempts = 1; internal/fsm/cli/deps.go:101 builds that exec with exec.CommandContext and no deadline, and a grep for WithTimeout/WithDeadline across cmd/ and internal/ finds only internal/fsm/judge/judge.go:564 (the HTTP arm) and internal/fsm/cmdexec/cmdexec.go:229. So a `codex exec` that hangs (stalled OAuth refresh, upstream stall) hangs the FSM run forever with no bound, and a single transient CLI failure is fatal where the same failure over HTTP would be retried five times with backoff. The convergence budget atom counts tokens, not wall clock, so nothing else stops it. This is an undocumented asymmetry between two providers the spec treats as swappable.

findings.note: itoa (internal/fsm/judge/codex.go:142) reimplements strconv.Itoa to avoid an import that costs nothing (strconv is already in the binary transitively) and is wrong for math.MinInt: n = -n overflows back to a negative value, the digit loop never runs, and the function returns "-". Unreachable today because the only inputs are process exit codes, but it is untested at that boundary (codex_test.go:227 covers 0, 7, 42, -3, 1234567).

findings.note: DiffRuns collapses judge calls that share (node, iter, kind, input_hash) but differ in Index: internal/fsm/machine/diff.go:83 builds the map key without Index, and diff.go:91 overwrites row.A/row.B on a repeat, so the earlier call is silently dropped from the report. internal/fsm/kind/kind.go:445 and :590 emit indexed calls per candidate and per bug within one node+iter, so two identical candidate texts or two identically-worded bugs produce one row instead of two and the diff under-reports the calls made. The alignment key matches spec 3 section 4 as written, so this may be a spec bug rather than a code bug, but the report is lossy either way.
